title: Under the weather: two friends talk about health

script.text: Jack! You're back at school. I heard you'd been off for nearly two weeks.
Ten days, actually, though it felt like a month. I caught the flu from my little sister, and I've been in bed with a high temperature since the Monday before last.
Poor you. Were you taking any medicine?
Only paracetamol. My mum wanted me to see a doctor right away, but I said I'd wait a couple of days. In the end she dragged me to the clinic on Thursday.
Good for her. What did the doctor say?
That I'd been run-down for weeks and the flu just finished me off. She asked about my sleep, and I admitted that I go to bed at one or two. She wasn't impressed.
I'm not surprised. You're always on your phone at midnight.
It's only for homework, honestly. Well, mostly. Anyway, she told me to cut down on screen time and eat more regularly. I've been skipping breakfast for ages.
Seriously? My brother used to do that, and he was permanently tired.
He did, after our dad started cooking porridge every morning for a month. Now he says he can't live without it.
I'm not sure I'm ready for porridge. But I'd try fruit and yoghurt.
That's a start. What about exercise? You used to cycle everywhere.
I know, but the doctor says nothing strenuous for two weeks. I'm itching to start again. Staying in was driving me crazy.
Well, I'm going for a jog on Saturday. You could come for a short walk instead. Fresh air will do you good.
Maybe. Honestly, I'm more worried about the amount of homework I've missed. Mr Dawson promised to send me the notes, but I wouldn't hold my breath.
I can lend you mine. They're a mess, but they're complete.
That would be great. And a walk sounds nice. I should ask my mum first, though. She's quite strict at the moment.

statements: Jack has been absent from school for more than two weeks.
Jack's mother thought he should see a doctor as soon as he fell ill.
The doctor disapproved of Jack's sleeping habits.
Jack says that he uses his phone at night only for homework.
The doctor has limited the kind of exercise Jack can do for now.
Jack has already asked his mother whether he can go out with Olivia.
discuss: Which of Jack's habits is the most harmful in your opinion, and why?
How can teenagers cut down on screen time? Suggest three realistic ideas.
What do you do to stay healthy during exam season?
